check.name: lens.conventions
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

snippet.text: | `melian doctor` | Checks Node, git and `--attr-source`, Pi's login, providers with credentials, the GitHub token's source, gh, and the repository. It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable. Its `records` line, when the checkout has an `origin`, fetches the `melian/state` branch's tip into the store's own repository. It names, as a warning, up to five files on it that Melian did not write, which refuse calls until a writer removes them, or warns that the branch cannot be read. Opening the store sweeps what killed calls left in the state directory, and the line warns about what that sweep left: up to five leftovers it kept because it cannot tell their maker is gone, up to five of an exited call it could not remove, how many stale ones it ran out of time to remove, or left because it could not list every leftover, which the next open removes, that it stopped listing at its bound of 1,000 leftovers, and a process table it could not read, which sweeps nothing and keeps every leftover it found. It names them after the branch's own warning when the branch cannot be read, since the sweep ran when the store opened. A sweep that removed all it found says nothing. The same line then says whom the committed root policy trusts to write the branch. It reads `trust.writers` from the same base as the `trust` line. With it on, the line says the branch's writers are trusted as the repository's writers. With it off, it warns that only the trusted host may write `melian/state`, since doctor cannot check who may push to it. When no policy can be read, it warns that who may write the branch is unknown. A policy read from local `main` or `HEAD` makes the line a warning, with the `trust` line's caveat. Doctor reads the cached remote-tra [cut at 2 KiB]

message.text: The change adds a `packages` line to `melian doctor`. The line warns when Melian's install links outside itself or is not laid out as npm lays one out, and fails doctor, so it exits 1, when the install cannot be read. The doctor row in docs/guidelines/cli.md was not updated: it does not describe this line, and its list of exit-1 causes leaves this one out.

explanation.what: The change adds a `packages` line to `melian doctor`. The line warns when Melian's install links outside itself or is not laid out as npm lays one out, and fails doctor, so it exits 1, when the install cannot be read. The doctor row in docs/guidelines/cli.md was not updated: it does not describe this line, and its list of exit-1 causes leaves this one out.
explanation.whatToDo: In the doctor row, describe the `packages` line: what it names and when it warns. Add "Melian's install cannot be read" to the list of causes for exit `1`.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md says: "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented." packages/cli/AGENTS.md also says: "A new command, or a new exit code, goes into `usage` in `src/main.ts` and the table in the guideline together." The table is now wrong about when doctor exits 1.

properties.failureScenario: The user's install holds more than 50,000 directories, or holds an unreadable module path. `melianInstall()` throws, and doctor prints `fail packages ...` and exits 1, as the new test expects. A user who reads the guideline's table finds no cause that covers this exit 1, and no mention of the `packages` warning that says no review reuses a run.
